newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves US$107.5 mln foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves US$107.5 mln foreign investment.

text.p: Taiwan's economics ministry said on Monday it had approved four foreign investment projects in Taiwan worth a total of US$107.5 million.
The approvals include a plan by Britain's Asia Link Taiwan to invest US$62.182 million in a mobile phone operation joint venture called Smartlink, the ministry said in a statement.

Smartlink, headed by Taiwan's Tuntex Distinct Corp, won two regional operation licences in hotly contested open bidding in January that opened the island's long-monopolised mobile telephony sector to private investment.
Under liberalised rules, foreign investors can now own stakes of up to 20 percent in Taiwan telecom ventures.
In addition to the foreign investments, the ministry also approved 11 projects totalling $84.347 million in indirect Taiwanese investment in China.
It cleared food giant President Enterprises to pour an additional $12.24 million into its beer manufacturing and sales company in China's southern coastal special economic zone of Zhuhai.
Lien Hwa Industry Corp was granted approval to invest US$15 million in a mainland food company, the ministry added.
Taiwan, a rival with China since a civil war split them in 1949, bans direct trade with China and requires firms investing in the mainland to route projects through a third territory.

Despite the deep political divide, some 30,000 Taiwan businesses have poured over US$20 billion into China, making Taiwan one of China's leading overseas investors -- and China one of Taiwan's most important markets.

In a strategic shift from the second half of 1996, Taiwan's ruling Nationalist government said the economy must not become overdependent on communist China and urged firms to invest more in Taiwan itself or other overseas destinations.
